text:
Dylan Holloway is the Blue the numbers like more than the scoresheet does. He has 15 points in 21 games, but four goals on 7.1 expected (the quality of his chances), and his team has scored 5.1 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. That reads like bad luck, not a player in decline: St. Louis takes 55% of the expected goals at five on five when he plays, more than five points better than without him.

Last season was his breakout. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.8 wins, 20th among 401 forwards, though they also note his results ran ahead of his chances, so some regression was always coming. He is fast (94th percentile top speed), shoots hard, throws hits (48 already) and draws more penalties than he takes.

The last 10 games have been thin, five points on chances that would usually bring eight, and The Hockey Writers has argued the Blues should flip him and Jake Neighbours in the lineup. Watch the shooting percentage: 8.2% now, against a range for him that centers near 13%.
